audit_event.notes: Per Requirement 7.2.1 the cascade marks every descendant of the parent as Revoked in the same transaction; per 7.2.2 no new DELEGATE referencing the Revoked parent may succeed. Per 7.2.3 RR pushes REVOKE notifications to RPs of every cascaded child within RevocationVisibilityBudget.

irreversibility_note: Cascade revocation is just as irreversible as direct revocation: every descendant's status becomes terminal-Revoked. To resume operations the HP must run BOOTSTRAP again, yielding a fresh root Mandate with a new mandate_id (Requirement 4.3.3).
notes: Tree depth 2 satisfies the task-3.5 acceptance criterion ‘cascade=true 级联派生树 + 子 Mandate 撤销结果, 深度 2’. Validates Requirement 7.2.1 (atomic cascade), 7.2.2 (no further DELEGATE off Revoked parent), and 7.2.3 (RR push to every affected RP).

signature_verification.note: REVOKE envelope is signed by HP (Requirement 4.1.3 — REVOKE auth-strength ≥ BOOTSTRAP auth-strength). REVOKE_RECEIPT / ERROR is signed by MS. Both envelopes use canonical CBOR as signing input regardless of wire encoding.

summary: Cascade REVOKE on a depth-2 derivation tree (parent G3 → child G2 → grandchild G1). One REVOKE on the parent atomically marks both descendants as Revoked and the receipt enumerates them in topological order.
